items.title: vLLM posts the best DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash result on SemiAnalysis AgentX: 954K tokens/s per GPU on a GB300 NVL72 rack
items.summary: On SemiAnalysis AgentX, a benchmark built from real agentic workloads, vLLM serves DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash at 954K total tokens/s per GPU (cached, input and output) with 196 tokens/s P90 per user. That works out to $38.96 of revenue per GPU-hour at DeepSeek's off-peak prices. The setup uses prefill/decode disaggregation and wide expert parallelism across a GB300 NVL72 rack, 7.9x vLLM's single-node result. The engineering blog covers the work and how to reproduce it. This is separate from the DeepInfer decode-parity post kept at 18:04Z.

doubt.source: Self-reported by the vLLM team; no independent SemiAnalysis post seen yet.

items.title: Generative Value Classifier (Stanford): a robot RL critic that learns from actions, reaching about 85% on RoboMimic Tool Hang where QC and RLPD stall near 50%
items.summary: Swerdlow, Dong and Finn treat value learning as generative classification. A return-conditioned flow policy scores each action against a set of return bins, and Bayes' rule turns those scores into a Q-function, so every action in the data trains the critic. Online on RoboMimic Tool Hang, GVC gets to about 85% success within 0.5M steps, while QC and RLPD reach about 50% at 1M. Offline on OGBench (35 tasks, 8 seeds), it scores 98% vs 86% for BFN on scene-sparse and 41% vs 32% on puzzle-4x4. In offline-to-online runs, it goes from 67.1% to 98.9% on average. The cost: an update is about 5 to 9x slower than a scalar regression critic (15.6 ms on an H100).

items.title: Open-source eGPU setup splits Llama 3.3 70B across an Intel Arc B60 and an NVIDIA 5060 on one MacBook Pro running Linux
items.summary: A builder posts a working setup that runs one Llama 3.3 70B model split across two external GPUs from different vendors, an Intel B60 and an NVIDIA 5060. Both are attached to an Apple Silicon MacBook Pro running Linux (Omarchy). The repo is open source. The post gives no throughput numbers.

doubt.source: Single builder report with no performance numbers; not reproduced.
